settings.title: Add a package in three steps

items.title: Create a SCORM lesson
items.description: In a course, add a lesson, choose the SCORM type, give it a title and save it.

items.title: Upload your ZIP
items.description: CourseLit checks the package and shows its title, version and file count.

items.title: Learners enter the activity
items.description: Learners select Enter SCORM content, which opens the activity in a separate window.

settings.title: What your package needs
settings.body:
- A SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004 package in ZIP format
- Under 300 MB
- An `imsmanifest.xml` file at the top level of the ZIP, with an entry point (a launch file) listed in it

If a package is rejected, CourseLit tells you why, for example that the manifest or the launch file is missing.

A learner cannot mark a SCORM lesson complete until the package has reported progress, such as a completed status or a recorded interaction.

[Certificates](/docs/products/certificates)

settings.title: Honest about Alpha
settings.body:
The SCORM lesson type is marked **Alpha** in the lesson editor. Before you sell a SCORM course, invite yourself with a second email address and work through the lesson as a learner.

On the cloud, SCORM is part of the **Business** plan. Self-hosted CourseLit includes it with every other feature.

[See pricing](/pricing)

items.question: Which SCORM versions are supported?
items.answer: SCORM 1.2 and SCORM 2004, uploaded as a ZIP package of up to 300 MB.

items.question: Do SCORM lessons count toward certificates?
items.answer: Yes. A course issues its certificate when the learner has completed every live lesson, and a SCORM lesson counts once the package has reported progress.

items.question: Which plan includes SCORM?
items.answer: Business on the cloud. Self-hosted CourseLit includes it with every other feature.

items.question: Is SCORM ready for production?
items.answer: The lesson type is marked Alpha. Test your package as a learner before you sell the course.
